scope: Inspection against the saved case criteria. Explanation/code structure and Python syntax were checked, but generated code and numerical reconciliation were not run.
comparison_note: There is one sample per case. The open-trade input and criteria also changed, so improvements for that case reflect the combined prompt and case changes.
line_numbering: Findings cite 1-based lines of each record's response text.

findings: The previous discarded placeholder loop is absent. The response uses full rolling windows, next-Open fills, and no last-bar Close fallback.

Line 269 computes average_loss using closed_trades[closed_trades["realized_pnl"]]. The inner expression supplies numeric P&L values as DataFrame column selectors rather than a boolean mask. This expression is evaluated when any closed trade exists, breaking the closed-trade summary path before the function can return.
The case therefore does not provide a complete usable backtest. Numerical reconciliation of logged fills and strategy results remains unverified.
Lines 81-90 reject noninteger inputs, zero or negative fast/slow windows, and slow < fast before the rolling calculations at lines 125-126.
The ordering check uses slow < fast, so equal positive windows remain allowed.
This pass applies only to the listed window-validation rules, based on static inspection; it does not validate the entire generated backtest.
Lines 129-160 and 164-200 leave final-bar entry and exit signals unfilled. There is no last-bar Close fill fallback.
The code waits for complete moving-average windows and checks both previous and current averages before detecting crossovers.
Lines 142-151 initialize exit and realized fields as None. Lines 202-217 append an unfinished trade once, preserve its entry, and compute unrealized P&L separately.

The listed open-trade behavior passes static review for the default qty=1. An additional defect remains outside that default: lines 186 and 213 divide quantity-scaled P&L only by entry_price, so reported return fractions scale with qty and disagree with the explanation's price-return formulas when qty differs from 1.
This scoped pass does not establish runtime behavior or general trading correctness.
